title: Halves into quarters
line: A bar cut in half gets sliced again, and 1/2 turns into 2/4 while the shaded part stays exactly the same size.

title: Bigger bottom, smaller slice
line: Three identical pizzas split into 3, 4 and 8 slices, then one slice from each lines up to show 1/3 > 1/4 > 1/8.

title: Same spot on the line
line: Dots for 2/3 and 4/6 drop onto a number line cut in thirds and one cut in sixths, landing at the same point.

title: Fractions that equal one
line: Bars for 2/2, 3/3, 4/4 and 6/6 fill one piece at a time, and every one of them finishes as a full whole.

title: Marching by thirds
line: A hop of length 1/3 copies itself along a number line from 0, landing on 1/3, 2/3, 3/3, then past 1 at 4/3.

title: A bar becomes a line
line: A fraction bar shaded 5/8 squashes flat onto a number line, and its right edge turns into the point 5/8.

title: Building three fifths
line: A ribbon splits into 5 equal pieces, one piece lifts out labeled 1/5, then 3 copies line up into 3/5.

title: That's not a fourth
line: A square cut into 4 uneven strips is labeled 1/4, the strips slide together to show they differ, then the cuts even out.

title: The shrinking slice
line: As the bottom number ticks from 2 up to 12, a circle gets more slices and the one highlighted slice keeps getting thinner.

title: Four ways to halve a square
line: A square is halved four different ways, and each time one half spins onto the other and fits exactly.

title: Hexagon into sixths
line: A hexagon splits into 6 triangles, then 3 rhombuses, then 2 trapezoids, and every piece gets its fraction label.

title: Weird-looking quarters
line: A 4×4 grid splits into 4 zigzag pieces of 4 squares each, and counting squares proves each strange piece is 1/4.

title: Quadrilateral family circles
line: Shapes drop into a big quadrilateral circle, and a square slides into the overlap where the rectangle and rhombus circles meet.

title: Squash a square
line: A square's corners get dragged: lean it and it's a rhombus, stretch it and it's a rectangle, tug one corner and it's neither.

title: Same fence, different yards
line: A loop of 20 fence units reshapes into 1×9, 2×8, 3×7, 4×6 and 5×5 rectangles while an area counter climbs to 25.

title: Twelve squares, many fences
line: Twelve unit squares rearrange into 1×12, 2×6 and 3×4 rectangles, and the perimeter counter drops from 26 to 14.

title: The missing side
line: A pentagon's perimeter reads 30, four sides light up as 5, 7, 6 and 4, and the last side counts out as 8.

title: Tile, then multiply
line: Unit squares tile a 4×6 rectangle row by row, the counter hits 24, then the rows collapse into the label 4 × 6.

title: Splitting a rectangle
line: A 3×7 rectangle pulls apart into 3×5 and 3×2 pieces showing 15 + 6, then snaps back together as 21.

title: The L-shaped room
line: An L-shaped floor plan slices into two rectangles, each area counts up, then a different slice gives the same total.

title: Big squares, small squares
line: A rectangle measures 6 big squares, then each big square splits into 4 small ones and the count jumps to 24.

title: No gaps, no overlaps
line: Unit squares try to cover a 3×3 square, first with gaps, then overlapping, then snap into a clean grid that counts 9.

title: Six squares, any shape
line: Six unit squares slide from a 2×3 rectangle into a cross, a staircase and a long line, and the area stays 6.

title: Pencils to a line plot
line: Ten pencils line up against a ruler marked in quarter inches, and each length drops an X onto a line plot above it.

title: Pictures melt into bars
line: Fruit icons worth 2 votes each stack into a picture graph, melt into bars, and a brace measures how many more chose apples.

title: Filling the liter jug
line: Beakers holding 250, 400 and 350 mL pour into a 1 liter jug, and the water climbs to exactly the 1 L mark.

title: Minutes on a number line
line: A clock's minute hand sweeps from 2:15 to 3:05 while a number line below hops 45 minutes, then 5 more, totaling 50.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten

line: Nine stacks of 8 ten-rods regroup into 72 tens, then bundle into 7 hundred-squares and 2 rods, showing 9 × 80 = 720.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Squares become strips
line: A 6×4 rectangle of 24 squares stretches into 6×40 as every square becomes a strip of ten, and 24 becomes 240.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Blocks that regroup
line: Base-ten blocks for 347 and 285 merge, 12 ones snap into a ten, 13 tens snap into a hundred, and 632 is left.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Back 200, forward 2
line: On an open number line, 523 − 198 becomes one big jump back 200 and a small hop forward 2, landing on 325.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Cracking a hundred
line: To take 268 from 503, a hundred block cracks into tens, a ten cracks into ones, and 235 is left standing.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Rolling to the nearest ten
line: A ball at 47 sits on a hilly number line with valleys at every ten, and it rolls downhill into 50.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Zoom out to hundreds
line: The number 683 sits on a line marked in tens, the line zooms out to hundreds, and 683 snaps to 700.

title: Squares on the diagonal
line: A 10×10 times table lights up its diagonal 1, 4, 9, 16, and each number grows into an actual square of dots.

title: Where the evens live
line: Every even product in the times table turns blue, rows for 2, 4, 6 and 8 fill completely, and odd × odd stays white.

title: The nines trick
line: Multiples of 9 stack up, the tens digit climbs 1, 2, 3 while the ones digit falls 8, 7, 6, always summing to 9.

title: Bags of marbles
line: Three bags of 8 marbles stack into a bar of 24, a piece of 5 snips off, and the unknown n fills in as 19.

title: One array, four facts
line: A 40-dot array rotates and regroups so one picture reads as 8 × 5, 5 × 8, 40 ÷ 5 and 40 ÷ 8.

title: Nines from tens
line: A 10×7 array appears and one column fades out, turning 70 into 63 and showing 9 × 7 without memorizing it.

title: Doubling up to eights
line: A 2×6 array copies itself into 4×6, then 8×6, and the counter doubles each time: 12, 24, 48.

title: Division as a missing side
line: A rectangle of 56 squares has one side labeled 8, and the other side grows one column at a time until it reads 7.

title: Turn the array
line: A 3×5 array of dots rotates a quarter turn into 5×3, and the counter beside it never budges from 15.

title: Two ways to group 24
line: Two 3×4 dot grids slide together into one 6×4 grid, showing (2 × 3) × 4 and 2 × (3 × 4) both make 24.

title: What's in the cups
line: For ? ÷ 4 = 9, four cups of 9 dots pour into one pile that counts up to 36.

title: Eggs into cartons
line: Forty-two eggs roll in and fill cartons of 6, and the carton count reaches 7 as the last egg settles.

title: Cutting the ribbon
line: A 24 cm ribbon gets cut into 3 cm pieces that hop off one at a time, and the counter stops at 8.

title: Dealing 56 cards
line: Fifty-six cards deal out one at a time to 8 players around a table until each player holds 7.

title: Scoops of eight
line: A pile of 56 marbles loses 8 at a time to a scoop, and a tally counts 7 scoops until the pile is gone.

title: Five bags of seven
line: Five bags each spill 7 dots, the dots line up into a 5×7 array, and a counter ticks up to 35.

title: Frog jumps of seven
line: A frog makes 5 jumps of 7 along a number line, landing on 7, 14, 21, 28 and finally 35.

title: Decimal grid face-off
line: 0.4 and 0.38 shade on two hundred-grids, and 0.4's four full columns beat 0.38's three columns plus 8 squares.

title: Check the whole first
line: 0.3 of a huge square and 0.5 of a tiny square shade side by side, and the smaller decimal covers more area.

title: Tenths on a meter stick
line: A meter-long bar splits into 10 pieces, then 100, and a marker sliding along it reads 0.7, then 0.73.

title: Tenths into hundredths
line: A grid with 3/10 shaded has each column cut into 10 squares, becoming 30/100, then 25/100 more makes 55/100.

title: Three helpings of two thirds
line: Three bars each shaded 2/3 slide their pieces into one row of thirds, which counts to 6/3 and fills exactly 2 wholes.

title: Five scoops of flour
line: A 3/4 cup scoop pours 5 times into a jug marked in quarters, and the level climbs to 15/4, which is 3 3/4.

title: Many ways to make 5/8
line: Five one-eighth pieces split as 1/8 + 4/8, then 2/8 + 3/8, then 1/8 + 1/8 + 3/8, a gap sliding along the bar.

title: Unpacking a mixed number
line: The mixed number 2 1/3 unpacks as two whole bars burst into thirds, and all the pieces count up to 7/3.

title: Quarters make a whole
line: Bars for 1 3/4 and 2 2/4 join, four loose quarters snap into an extra whole, and the total reads 4 1/4.

title: Race to one half
line: Points for 3/8 and 5/9 slide along a number line toward a flag at 1/2, and one stops short while the other passes it.

title: Cut both into twelfths
line: Bars for 2/3 and 3/4 get sliced into twelfths, become 8/12 and 9/12, and 3/4 wins by one thin sliver.

title: Crossed cuts
line: Squares showing 2/5 in columns and 3/7 in rows each borrow the other's cuts, so both count in 35ths: 14 versus 15.

title: Slice it the other way
line: A square with 2 of 3 columns shaded gets cut into 4 rows, so 2/3 becomes 8/12 while the shaded area holds still.

title: Equivalent fractions in a line
line: 2/3, 4/6, 6/9 and 8/12 plot as dots at (bottom, top) on a grid, and they all land on one straight line through zero.

title: Flip along the fold
line: A heart, a letter A and a hexagon each flip across a dashed line, and their halves land exactly on each other.

title: Counting mirror lines
line: A dashed line spins inside a triangle, square, pentagon and hexagon, flashing at each symmetry line: 3, 4, 5, then 6 flashes.

title: The fake symmetry
line: A parallelogram tries flipping across its diagonal and its middle line, and both times the halves miss each other.

title: Right angle detector
line: A small square corner slides around a pile of triangles, glowing green at right angles, then the triangles sort into two groups.

title: Parallel side hunt
line: Pairs of parallel arrows sweep across a trapezoid, a parallelogram, a rectangle and a kite, lighting up sides that never meet.

title: Segment, ray, line
line: A dot stretches into a segment, one end shoots off as a ray, then both ends run forever as a line.

title: Opening angle
line: Two rays share an endpoint and one swings open, its label switching from acute to right at 90° to obtuse past it.

title: Angles snap together
line: A 30° wedge and a 45° wedge slide together at a shared corner, and the arc label counts up to 75°.

title: What's left of a line
line: A straight line has 130° marked, and the leftover gap fills in as its counter ticks down from 180 to 50°.

title: The opening fan
line: A fan of six 15° wedges opens one wedge at a time, the total reading 15, 30, 45 all the way to 90.

title: Reading the protractor
line: A protractor slides onto an angle, centers on the corner, and a needle sweeps along the scale from 0 to read 127°.

title: 360 tiny slices
line: A circle splits into 360 thin slices, then 90 of them light up together and form a perfect right angle.

title: An angle is a turn
line: A ray turns around its endpoint, tracing an arc, while the arc's fraction of the full circle counts up in degrees.

title: The snail race plot
line: Ten snails crawl distances like 3/8, 1/2 and 5/8 inch, each dropping an X on a line plot, then a brace measures the spread.

title: Width on a slider
line: A rectangle's width slides from 2 to 8 while its height stays 3, and both area and perimeter readouts update as it moves.

title: Pouring two liters
line: A 2 L bottle relabels itself as 2000 mL, then pours into 8 equal cups that each read 250 mL.

title: Zooming into a meter
line: A meter bar zooms in to 100 centimeters, one centimeter zooms in to 10 millimeters, and a two-column table fills in.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Dealing out 157
line: Base-ten blocks for 157 deal into 4 equal piles, a hundred cracks into tens along the way, and 1 leftover stays out.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Building the missing width
line: A rectangle of area 852 and height 4 builds its width in chunks of 200, then 10, then 3, reaching 213.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Four boxes make 23 × 14
line: A 23×14 rectangle splits into 20×10, 20×4, 3×10 and 3×4 pieces whose areas 200, 80, 30 and 12 add to 322.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Four copies of 1,236
line: Four copies of 1,236 in base-ten blocks merge, ones and tens regroup upward, and the pile settles at 4,944.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: The odometer
line: An odometer rolls 4,689 forward by 1,527, each wheel nudging the next as it passes 9, and stops at 6,216.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Round to any place
line: The point 47,382 sits on a number line that zooms out three times, snapping to 47,380, then 47,400, then 47,000.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Expanded form burst
line: The number 6,047 bursts into 6000 + 0 + 40 + 7, each piece flying out of its digit's column and back again.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Digit-by-digit duel
line: 58,312 and 58,293 compare from the left, matching digits turn grey one by one, until 3 beats 2 in the hundreds.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Ten makes the next
line: Ten ones snap into a rod, ten rods into a flat, ten flats into a long bar, each step ten times bigger.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: A 3 moving left
line: The digit 3 slides left through 3, 30, 300 and 3000, and a bar beside it grows ten times longer at each step.

title: Odd, even, odd, even
line: The rule add 3 from 1 builds 1, 4, 7, 10, and the numbers flash odd, even, odd, even, which the rule never said.

title: Matchstick triangles
line: Matchstick triangles in a row grow one at a time, sharing sides, and the stick count goes 3, 5, 7, 9.

title: Staircases become rectangles
line: Dot staircases grow 1, 3, 6, 10, and two copies of each one flip and snap together into a rectangle.

title: Every rectangle of 24
line: Twenty-four tiles rearrange into every rectangle they can, 1×24, 2×12, 3×8, 4×6, listing all the factor pairs.

title: Primes won't fit
line: Thirteen tiles try every rectangle and keep leaving one tile sticking out, while 12 tiles snap neatly into rows.

title: The sieve to 100
line: A 10×10 grid of 1 to 100 crosses out multiples of 2, 3, 5 and 7 in waves, leaving the primes glowing.

title: One more van
line: Twenty-nine kids board vans that seat 6, four vans fill up, 5 kids are left standing, and a fifth van rolls in.

title: Three times vs three more
line: A bar of 4 gets two partners, one 3 times as long and one 3 longer, and 12 and 7 line up side by side.

title: Stretching to 35
line: A bar of 7 stretches to 5 times its length, reaching 35, then a bar of 5 stretches 7 times to the same mark.

title: Fifths in three pizzas
line: Three pizzas cut into fifths, the slices pop out and line up, and the counter reaches 15 for 3 ÷ 1/5.

title: Sharing half a cake
line: Half a cake gets split among 3 people, the cuts extend across the whole cake, and each slice turns out to be 1/6.

title: One and a half recipes
line: A bar of 2/3 cup sugar grows by half of itself again for 1 1/2 recipes and lands on exactly 1 cup.

title: The scaling slider
line: A bar of length 6 gets multiplied by a sliding factor, shrinking when the factor drops under 1 and stretching when it's over.

title: Which side of 9
line: Arrows for 9 × 4/5 and 9 × 5/4 land on opposite sides of 9 on a number line before any arithmetic happens.

title: A fraction of a fraction
line: A square shaded 3/4 across gets cut 2/3 down, and the overlap of 6 small boxes out of 12 is 3/4 × 2/3.

title: Tiny tiles
line: A 2/3 by 5/2 rectangle fills with tiles 1/3 wide and 1/2 tall, and the tiles count up to 10 sixths.

title: Two thirds of twelve
line: Twelve dots split into 3 equal groups, 2 groups light up, and their 8 dots slide out as 2/3 of 12.

title: Three pizzas, four friends
line: Three pizzas get shared by 4 friends, each pizza cut in quarters, and every friend collects 3 quarters, so 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4.

title: Seven meters in three
line: A 7 meter ribbon is cut into 3 equal parts, and each piece lands on a ruler at 2 1/3 meters.

title: Estimate, then check
line: Bars for 2/5 and 1/2 snap to nearby benchmarks, the estimate lands just under 1, then the exact 9/10 confirms it.

title: Halves meet thirds
line: Pieces of 1/2 and 1/3 join end to end, and only after both get recut into sixths does the total read 5/6.

title: Breaking a whole to subtract
line: From 3 1/4 take 1 2/3: a whole cracks into twelfths, pieces disappear, and 1 7/12 is left.

title: Shape family tree
line: A tree grows from polygon down to quadrilateral, parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus and square, each branch showing a shape morphing into the next.

title: Inherited properties
line: A parallelogram's tag 'opposite sides parallel' copies itself down onto a rectangle, a rhombus and a square as each one appears.

title: Plant growth plot
line: A plant's height each week drops a dot onto a grid, and connecting the dots shows which week it grew fastest.

title: Treasure map path
line: A pirate walks a grid from (1, 2) to (4, 2) to (4, 6), and the distance of each leg counts out as it goes.

title: Walking to a point
line: A dot walks 3 units along the x-axis, then 5 units up, leaving a trail, and lands on the label (3, 5).

title: Order matters
line: Two dots follow the directions (2, 5) and (5, 2) at the same time and end up in completely different places.

title: Layer by layer
line: A 4×3 base of squares appears, then copies stack upward as layers of a box drawn at an angle until 5 layers make 60.

title: Two boxes make an L
line: An L-shaped block splits into a 3×2×4 box and a 2×2×2 box, whose volumes 24 and 8 add to 32.

title: Big cubes, small cubes
line: A box packs with 8 big cubes, then each big cube splits into 8 small ones, and the count jumps to 64.

title: Evening out the beakers
line: Eight beakers with 1/8, 1/4 and 1/2 liter make a line plot, then all the water pours together and shares out evenly.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Overflowing grids
line: 1.35 + 0.78 shades onto hundred-grids, hundredths overflow into a tenth, tenths overflow into a whole, giving 2.13.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Decimal times decimal
line: A 0.6 by 0.4 rectangle is cut from a unit square, and its overlap covers exactly 24 hundredths, so 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.24.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Quarters in two
line: A ruler of length 0.25 hops along a 2-unit bar, the counter reaching 8, so 2 ÷ 0.25 = 8.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Chipping away at 1,000
line: Groups of 32 peel off 1,000 in chunks of ten groups, then one at a time, tallying 31 groups with 8 left over.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Area model to algorithm
line: The area model for 327 × 46 splits into rows of 1,962 and 13,080, which slide into the standard algorithm and add to 15,042.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: More digits, not bigger
line: 0.7, 0.65 and 0.649 build as bars of tenths, hundredths and thousandths, and the one with fewest digits is longest.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Piling up zeros
line: 7 gets multiplied by 10, then 100, then 1000, a bar grows each time, and the powers of ten count the zeros.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: The point holds still
line: In 4.56 × 10, the decimal point stays put while every digit slides one place left, making 45.6, then 456.

topic: Number and Operations in Base Ten
title: Zooming into a hundred
line: A hundred-square zooms in: one strip is a tenth of it, one square of that strip is a tenth again, and so on.

title: Two rules, one line
line: Rules add 3 and add 6 build two lists from 0, and their pairs (3, 6), (6, 12) plot on one straight line.

title: Three times as big
line: The expression 3 × (18,932 + 921) draws as one long bar, then three copies stack up so it's clearly triple, with nothing calculated.

title: Parentheses change the answer
line: 2 + 3 × 4 builds as 2 dots plus 3 rows of 4, then (2 + 3) × 4 rebuilds as 5 rows: 14 vs 20.

title: Mean as a balance point
line: Seven dots sit on a seesaw number line, and the pivot slides back and forth until it balances exactly at the mean, 6.

title: One outlier drags the mean
line: A tenth dot flies out to 95, dragging the mean marker far to the right while the median marker barely twitches.

title: Mean distance, laid end to end
line: Each dot drops a segment to the mean, the segments line up end to end, then split evenly into the MAD.

title: Dot plot becomes a box plot
line: Fifteen dots split at the median and quartiles, then a box and whiskers grow around them as the dots fade away.

title: Dots melt into a histogram
line: Twenty stacked dots slide into bins of width 5 and fuse into solid bars, turning a dot plot into a histogram.

title: Same mean, different spread
line: Two rows of five dots both balance at 10, then one row stretches outward while its mean marker stays frozen.

title: Nine values, one number
line: Nine dots slide together and merge into a single dot at their mean, then a bracket grows back out showing their spread.

title: Dice sums build a hill
line: Two dice roll again and again, each sum dropping a dot above 2 through 12, until a triangle-shaped pile peaks at 7.

title: Dragging out a tail
line: A symmetric hill of dots gets pulled one dot at a time to the right until it leans with a long right tail.

title: Taxi fare table becomes a line
line: Rows of a taxi fare table, 3 dollars plus 2 per mile, fly onto axes as dots until a straight line appears.

title: Filling tank, climbing graph
line: Water fills a tank at 4 liters a minute while a dot climbs beside it, tracing y = 4x as the tank rises.

title: Every number bigger than 3
line: Dots land at 3.5, 4, 10, 3.01 and more, packing tighter until they melt into a solid arrow from an open circle.

title: Open circle or closed
line: A point creeps toward 5 under x < 5 and the circle stays hollow, then the sign becomes ≤ and the circle fills in.

title: Balance scale algebra
line: A mystery box and 3 weights balance 8 weights, 3 come off each side, and the box is left balancing 5.

title: Tape diagram for 4x = 28
line: A 28-unit bar splits into 4 equal pieces, then one piece lifts out and its length counts up to 7.

title: x is every number at once
line: The letter x flickers through 1, 2, 3, 4 while 3x + 1 beside it updates, one expression covering every case.

title: Perimeter of any square
line: A square grows and shrinks with side s, and its perimeter 4s counts along as a dot traces the border.

title: Testing candidates
line: Numbers 1 through 6 drop into 2x + 3 = 11, each wrong one bouncing off red until 4 locks in green.

title: A trail of true values
line: A point slides from 0 to 6 while the inequality glows green then red, leaving a green trail that becomes the solution set.

title: Always the same number
line: 3(x + 2) and 3x + 6 sit side by side while x spins through 0, 1, 5, and 12, and both outputs always match.

title: Fooled by one value
line: 2x and x² both give 4 when x is 2, then x slides to 3 and the match breaks apart: 6 versus 9.

title: Distributing with a rectangle
line: A 3 by (x + 2) rectangle splits into a 3x piece and a 6 piece, so 3(x + 2) becomes 3x + 6.

title: Sorting like terms
line: Scattered tiles for x + 3 + 2x + 1 slide into two piles, x tiles with x tiles and ones with ones, giving 3x + 4.

title: Order of operations tree
line: 2 + 3 × 4² collapses one step at a time as a tree, exponent first, then times, then plus, ending at 50.

title: Celsius to Fahrenheit machine
line: Temperatures 0, 20, and 100 drop into a machine labeled F = 9C/5 + 32 and come out 32, 68, and 212 on a thermometer.

title: Doubling by folding
line: A square splits in half, then every piece splits again, ten times over, while a counter climbs 2, 4, 8 up to 1024.

title: Three cubed from three squared
line: A 3 by 3 grid of dots shows 3², then two more copies slide in beside it to make 3³ = 27 dots.

title: Counting steps across zero
line: A dot walks from (−3, 2) to (4, 2) one step at a time while a counter ticks to 7, which is 3 + 4.

title: Rectangle across four quadrants
line: Four points, one in each quadrant, connect into a rectangle, and each side length pops out from its coordinates as a brace.

title: Absolute value as distance
line: Points at −6 and 4 each stretch a band back to 0, then the bands lie side by side and −6's is longer.

title: Bigger but less
line: 10 > 2 on a number line, then both points flip to −10 and −2, swapping order as the inequality sign flips too.

title: Opposite of the opposite
line: A point at 3 flips over 0 to −3, then flips again and lands back on 3 as −(−3) = 3 writes itself.

title: Signs flip, point reflects
line: Point (2, 3) mirrors across the y-axis to (−2, 3), then across the x-axis to (−2, −3), its signs changing as it lands.

title: Two number lines make a plane
line: A number line copies itself, the copy swings up to vertical through 0, and a grid fills in to make the coordinate plane.

title: Sea level is zero
line: A vertical number line becomes the sea: a diver sinks to −20, a gull rises to 15, and 0 is the waterline.

title: GCF by chopping squares
line: A 24 by 36 rectangle chops off the biggest squares it can, until 12 by 12 squares tile the leftover exactly: GCF 12.

title: Two frogs meet at the LCM
line: Two frogs hop along a number line, one by 4s and one by 6s, until both land on the same spot at 12.

title: Pulling out a common factor
line: 36 dots and 8 dots each arrange into rows of 4, then join into one block showing 36 + 8 = 4(9 + 2).

title: Decimal multiplication as area
line: A 1.3 by 2.4 rectangle on a grid breaks into ones, tenths, and hundredths pieces that add up to 3.12.

title: Long division as sharing
line: 672 blocks get shared among 3 groups: hundreds split first, leftovers break into tens and ones, and each group ends with 224.

title: How many 3/4s fit in 2
line: Copies of a 3/4 bar slide along a 2-unit bar: two fit, and the leftover 1/2 is 2/3 of another, so 2 2/3.

title: Dividing by 1/3 triples
line: A 2-unit bar gets chopped into thirds and the piece count climbs to 6, then into fifths and it climbs to 10.

title: Double number line
line: Miles and hours number lines stretch in lockstep, 60 above 1, 120 above 2, as a slider finds 150 above 2.5.

title: Thirty out of a hundred
line: A 10 by 10 grid fills 30 squares, then rearranges onto a row of 50 people and 15 of them light up.

title: Finding the whole from 40%
line: A bar worth 12 is marked 40%, splits into four 3s, then six more 3s appear and the whole reads 30.

title: Price of one apple
line: A $6 bag of 4 apples splits open into 4 single apples, the price tag splitting with them into four $1.50 tags.

title: Which bag is the better deal
line: Bags of 5 for $3 and 8 for $4.40 each shrink down to one item, revealing 60 cents against 55 cents.

title: Three to two, forever
line: Three red and two blue squares copy themselves into rows, 6 to 4, then 9 to 6, while the color mix never changes.

title: Same shade of green
line: A cup mixes 2 scoops of blue with 3 of yellow; doubling both keeps the exact green, but one extra blue darkens it.

title: Box net, face by face
line: A flat net of six rectangles lights one face at a time, each area counting into a running surface area total.

title: Pyramid net petals
line: A square base with four triangle flaps: each flap swings out flat, its area adds to the base, and the total counts up.

title: Polygon from coordinates
line: Six points drop onto a grid and connect into an L-shaped hexagon, and each side length is read off by subtracting coordinates.

title: Parallelogram into rectangle
line: A triangle slices off one end of a parallelogram and slides to the other end, making a rectangle with equal base and height.

title: Triangle is half a parallelogram
line: A triangle gets a copy that spins 180 degrees and snaps on, forming a parallelogram exactly twice its area.

title: Trapezoid doubled
line: A trapezoid with bases 3 and 7 copies itself, flips, and joins to make a parallelogram with base 10, so half of that.

title: Three coin flips as a tree
line: A coin flip branches into H and T three times, and the 3 of 8 leaves with exactly two heads light up.

title: Double sixes in 36 cells
line: A 6 by 6 grid of dice pairs fills in, then only one corner cell lights up for double sixes: 1 in 36.

title: Spinner versus the tally
line: A spinner split 1/2, 1/4, 1/4 spins 40 times while bars of real counts wobble near the predicted heights.

title: Catching a loaded die
line: A die rolls 60 times, bars grow, one face towers over the rest, and the fair 1/6 model gets crossed out.

title: Coin flips settle down
line: A coin flips 500 times while a graph of the fraction of heads swings wildly at first, then settles onto 0.5.

title: Raindrops estimate pi
line: Random dots rain onto a square with a circle inside, and the fraction landing in the circle creeps toward 0.785, which is π/4.

title: From impossible to certain
line: Events slide onto a 0 to 1 line: rolling 7 on one die at 0, heads at 1/2, sunrise at 1.

title: Swapping marbles
line: Ten marbles swap from red to blue one by one while a pointer on a 0 to 1 line tracks the chance of red.

title: Sun plants versus shade plants
line: Two dot plots of plant heights stack up, mean markers drop onto each, and the gap between them reads 5 cm.

title: Pulling two piles apart
line: Two matching dot plots start on top of each other, then one slides right while the gap counts up in MADs: 1, 2, 3.

title: Sample results pile up
line: Twenty random samples of 10 beads are scooped from a jar, and each sample's percent red drops as a dot, piling up near 40%.

title: A biased scoop
line: From a grid of 100 dots, a sample grabbed from one corner shows 90% blue, while a scattered random sample shows the true 60%.

title: Running the machine backward
line: x passes through times 3, then plus 5, and comes out 20; the arrows reverse and carry 20 back to 5.

title: Dividing by a negative
line: Solving −2x > 6, both sides divide by −2, the number line mirrors across 0, and the solution arrow flips to x < −3.

title: A 5% raise is 1.05a
line: A bar of length a gets a 5% sliver glued to its end, then the whole bar relabels from a + 0.05a to 1.05a.

title: Zero pairs vanish
line: Tiles for 2x + 3 and −x − 5 pile together, opposite tiles pair up and vanish with a pop, leaving x − 2.

title: Factoring 6x + 9
line: Six x tiles and nine unit tiles regroup into 3 identical rows of 2x + 3, so 6x + 9 becomes 3(2x + 3).

title: Negative times negative
line: −3 times 3, 2, 1, 0, −1 gives dots at −9, −6, −3, 0, then 3, climbing by 3 each time, forcing a positive.

title: Why 1/7 repeats
line: Long division of 1 by 7 runs on screen, the remainders cycle 3, 2, 6, 4, 5, 1, and the digits 142857 loop forever.

title: Adding as an arrow
line: An arrow for −8 snaps onto a number line starting at 5 and ends at −3, then a +8 arrow carries it straight back.

title: Subtracting is adding the opposite
line: 7 − 3 and 7 + (−3) play out as arrows on two number lines side by side and finish at the same spot.

title: Distance is the difference
line: Points at −4 and 3 have a brace between them reading 7, and as both points slide around, the brace keeps matching |a − b|.

title: 20% off, then 20% on
line: A $100 bar shrinks 20% to 80, then grows 20% to 96, falling short because the second 20% is of a smaller bar.

title: Straight through the origin
line: Points for 3 cups of flour per 2 eggs line up through (0, 0), while points for y = 2x + 1 miss it.

title: Unit rate at x = 1
line: A dot slides along y = 2.5x to x = 1, and a dashed line drops to show the unit rate 2.5 sitting right there.

title: Half mile, quarter hour
line: A walker covers 1/2 mile in 1/4 hour, then the trip copies itself 4 times along the track: 2 miles per hour.

title: One L-shape, three ways
line: An L-shaped floor is cut across, cut down, then seen as a 6 by 5 rectangle minus a corner: 26 every time.

title: Vertical angles stay twins
line: Two crossing lines turn while the opposite angles of the X show matching readouts, 50 and 50, then 70 and 70.

title: Sweeping across a straight line
line: A ray sweeps across a straight line, one angle growing as the other shrinks, and their sum stays stuck at 180.

title: Circle into a rectangle
line: A circle cut into 16 wedges rearranges into a near-rectangle of width πr and height r, so the area is πr².

title: Rolling out pi
line: A circle with diameter 1 rolls along a number line, its rim leaving a trail that ends just past 3.14.

title: Peeling rings into a triangle
line: A circle's thin rings peel off, straighten into strips, and stack into a triangle with base 2πr and height r.

title: Sticks that can't close
line: Sticks of 3, 4, and 9 swing on hinges but never meet, then the 9 shrinks to 6 and the triangle snaps shut.

title: One swing, two triangles
line: A side of length 5 swings from a fixed corner and crosses the base line in two places, giving two different triangles.

title: Double scale, four times floor
line: A 2 by 3 room plan doubles to 4 by 6, and exactly four copies of the original slide in to fill it.

title: Bike ride as a graph
line: A rider goes out, stops, and comes home while a distance graph draws beside it: steep when fast, flat when stopped, falling back.

title: Filling a flask
line: Water fills a flask with a narrow neck, and the height graph bends upward as the level speeds up in the neck.

title: Two points make a line
line: Points (2, 7) and (5, 13) get a rise-over-run staircase of slope 2, then the line extends back to hit the y-axis at 3.

title: Burning candle
line: A 12 cm candle shrinks 1.5 cm each hour beside a graph whose line starts at 12 and hits zero at hour 8.

title: Equal steps or growing steps
line: y = 2x and y = x² plot together, and equal steps right give equal climbs for one and bigger climbs for the other.

title: Dialing m and b
line: In y = mx + b, dialing m from −2 to 3 tilts the line, then dialing b slides it up and down without turning.

title: A table races a graph
line: Runner A is a table and runner B is a graphed line; both race on a track and B overtakes at second 4.

title: One input, one output
line: Inputs drop into a machine and each pops out one output, then a broken machine spits two outputs for one input and turns red.

title: The vertical line test
line: A vertical line sweeps across a parabola touching it once each time, then across a sideways parabola where it hits twice.

title: Two-way table in percents
line: A table of 100 students by pet and phone fills in, then each row converts to percents and the rows clearly differ.

title: Reading the trend line
line: Plant heights by week get the line y = 2x + 3, a slider at week 7 reads 17 cm, and the 3 means starting height.

title: Spin the line to fit
line: A line rotates through a scatter plot while vertical gaps to each point stretch and shrink, and a total-gap counter bottoms out.

title: Scatter plots that change shape
line: A cloud of points morphs from rising, to falling, to no pattern, to a curve, with a label appearing for each shape.

title: Where two lines cross
line: Lines y = 2x + 1 and y = −x + 7 draw on axes, a dot rides each one, and the two dots meet at (2, 5).

title: Parallel, then the same line
line: Two lines with slope 3 never meet, then one slides its intercept until it merges with the other, giving infinitely many solutions.

title: Three ways an equation ends
line: Three equations simplify side by side and land on x = 4, then 5 = 5, then 3 = 7, each ending glowing a different color.

title: Expand, collect, solve
line: 3(x + 2) = x + 14 expands, x terms slide left and numbers slide right, until it shrinks to x = 4.

title: Slope triangles anywhere
line: A rise-run triangle slides along y = 2x + 1, stretching as it goes but staying similar, so rise over run always reads 2.

title: Slope is the price per pound
line: On the graph of $4 per pound, a step of 1 right and 4 up repeats into a staircase hugging the line.

title: Multiplying in scientific notation
line: (3 × 10⁴)(2 × 10⁵) splits apart, the 3 and 2 multiply, the exponents add, and 6 × 10⁹ assembles.

title: Powers of ten zoom out
line: A number line zooms out tenfold each step, from 1 to 10 to 100 all the way to 10⁹, as the exponent ticks up.

title: Building a million dots
line: A 10 by 10 grid of dots shrinks into one dot of a new 10 by 10 grid, three times over, reaching a million.

title: Square roots as sides
line: Squares of area 1, 4, 9, 16 line up by side length, then a square of area 2 squeezes in between 1 and 2.

title: Swinging the diagonal down
line: The diagonal of a unit square swings down onto a number line like a compass arm and lands at 1.414.

title: Exponents add by counting
line: 2³ × 2⁴ unpacks into three 2s and four 2s, the times sign dissolves, and seven 2s regroup into 2⁷.

title: Why 2⁰ is 1
line: A column of 16, 8, 4, 2 halves at each step down, so 2⁰ lands on 1 and 2⁻¹ lands on 1/2.

title: Closing in on √2
line: A zoom box narrows from 1.4 to 1.5, then 1.41 to 1.42, trapping √2 one digit at a time on a number line.

title: Ordering π, 3.15, and √10
line: π, 3.15, and √10 drop onto a number line near 3, and a zoom reveals the order: π, then 3.15, then √10.

title: 0.2727... becomes 3/11
line: x = 0.272727... copies itself as 100x, the endless tails line up and cancel, leaving 99x = 27, so x = 3/11.

title: Three cones fill a cylinder
line: Side views of a cone and cylinder with the same base and height: the cone pours three times and the cylinder fills exactly.

title: Distance by a hidden triangle
line: Points (1, 2) and (7, 10) sprout a right triangle with legs 6 and 8, and the hypotenuse measures 10.

title: Every point 5 away
line: A point sweeps around the origin at distance 5, and each time it hits a grid point like (3, 4) a right triangle flashes.

title: Sliding ladder
line: A 13-foot ladder slides down a wall, and when its foot is 5 feet out, a right triangle shows the top at 12 feet.

title: Pythagoras by rearranging
line: Four copies of a right triangle sit inside a big square, then slide around so the empty space changes from c² into a² + b².

title: Tiles refill the big square
line: Squares on legs 3 and 4 break into unit tiles that fly over and exactly refill the 5 by 5 square on the hypotenuse.

title: The converse on a hinge
line: Sticks of 3 and 4 hinged together open until the gap between their ends is exactly 5, and the angle reads 90 degrees.

title: Torn corners make a line
line: A triangle's three corners tear off and slide together along a line, fitting exactly into a straight 180 degree angle.

title: Sliding transversal
line: A transversal crosses two parallel lines and tilts back and forth, and its eight angles only ever show two values that add to 180.

title: Exterior angle filled
line: One side of a triangle extends past a corner, and the two far angles slide over to exactly fill the outside angle.

title: Two angles are enough
line: Two triangles with angles 30 and 70 start at different sizes, and one dilates until it lands exactly on the other.

title: Dilate, turn, land
line: A small triangle dilates by 2 from a center point, turns 90 degrees, and slides to land exactly on a larger triangle.

title: Moves with live coordinates
line: A triangle on a grid reflects, rotates, and dilates while its corner coordinates update live: (x, y) to (−x, y) to (2x, 2y).

title: Rotating swaps coordinates
line: Point (3, 1) rotates 90 degrees around the origin to (−1, 3), and a triangle traced through it turns along with it.

title: Snapping one shape onto another
line: Two matching arrow shapes sit on a plane, and the first slides, turns 120 degrees, then flips to snap exactly onto the second.

title: Rotations keep everything
line: Two parallel segments rotate around a point, and live readouts show their lengths and the angle between them never change.

title: Shading the half-plane
line: A dot wanders the plane, turning green when 2x + y < 4 and red otherwise, until green paints one whole side of the line.

title: Two shadows overlap
line: The half-planes y > x - 1 and y < -x + 3 shade in blue and yellow, and the wedge where they overlap turns green.

title: Dashed or solid boundary
line: The line y = 2x + 1 flips between dashed and solid as < becomes ≤, and dots sitting on the line switch on and off.

title: Zooming in on a crossing
line: y = 2^x and y = x + 3 cross near x = 2.44, and each zoom into the crossing adds one more correct digit.

title: The gap shrinks to zero
line: A vertical bar measures the gap between y = x² and y = 6 - x, shrinking to nothing exactly at x = 2 and x = -3.

title: Solutions fuse into a line
line: Pairs that solve x + y = 5 pop in as dots, (0,5), (1,4), (2.5,2.5), until hundreds of them merge into a solid line.

title: Points that pass the test
line: Random points flash across the plane, and only those with x² + y² = 25 stay, slowly drawing a circle of radius 5.

title: A dot that must obey
line: A dot slides along y = x² with its coordinates checked live, and the check turns red the moment it steps off the curve.

title: Undoing a matrix
line: A grid gets sheared and stretched by a 2×2 matrix, then the inverse matrix runs it backwards and every square snaps home.

title: Pulling the answer back
line: A matrix sends a mystery point to (5, 3), then the inverse transform drags (5, 3) back to reveal the answer (2, 1).

title: Two equations, one matrix
line: The numbers in 2x + 3y = 8 and x - y = -1 lift into a 2×2 box, and x and y slide into a column.

title: A line slicing a parabola
line: A line slides upward past y = x², touching it at zero, then one, then two points, with the crossing count shown on screen.

title: Substitute and watch
line: x + 2 flies into y = x², giving x² - x - 2 = 0, which factors and drops two dots at x = 2 and -1.

title: A ball lands on a ramp
line: A ball flies along y = -x² + 4x over a ramp y = x and touches down where they meet, at x = 3.

title: Tilting until parallel
line: One line rotates while the other stays put, and their crossing point races off screen as the slopes match: no solution.

title: Nickels and dimes by sliding
line: Ten coins worth 65 cents: a slider trades dimes for nickels, the total counts down, and it hits 65 at 7 nickels.

title: The y's collide
line: 3x + 2y = 16 stacks over x - 2y = 0, the +2y and -2y crash together and vanish, leaving 4x = 16, so x = 4.

title: Adding keeps the crossing
line: Lines x + y = 4 and x - y = 2 cross at (3, 1), and their sum 2x = 6 swings in through that same point.

title: A line pinned to a point
line: As k slides from -3 to 3, the line (x + y - 4) + k(x - y - 2) = 0 spins like a clock hand around (3, 1).

title: Stacking two balanced scales
line: Two balanced scales pour their contents onto one bigger scale, which stays perfectly level because both sides grew by equal amounts.

title: Completing an actual square
line: x² + 6x is a square plus two 3-wide strips; the strips fold onto two sides and a missing 3×3 corner fills in.

title: The formula builds itself
line: ax² + bx + c = 0 changes line by line, terms sliding across the equals sign, until the quadratic formula drops into place.

title: When the parabola misses
line: y = x² + 2x + c rises as c grows, its two roots slide together, merge at c = 1, then leave the x-axis entirely.

title: Two answers for 49
line: A 7×7 square of dots shows x² = 49, then both 7 and -7 light up, since (-7)² is also 49.

title: Why the inequality flips
line: -2x > 6 shades a number line, then multiplying by -1 mirrors the whole line around zero and the arrow swings to x < -3.

title: Letters instead of numbers
line: Sliders change a, b, c in ax + b = c, and (c - b)/a updates as a dot tracks it on a number line.

title: The square root that lied
line: Squaring √(x + 2) = x gives roots 2 and -1, but plugging -1 back in makes √1 = -1 flash red: a fake answer.

title: An answer that divides by zero
line: Solving x/(x - 3) = 3/(x - 3) gives x = 3, then the denominator counts down to 0 and the answer cracks apart.

title: Each line keeps the promise
line: 2x + 3 = 11 changes one step at a time, both sides getting the same move, with arrows linking each line back to the last.

title: Running the machine backwards
line: A number goes through ×3 then -5 and comes out 16; the solver runs it backwards, +5 then ÷3, and 7 pops out.

title: Pulling r out of A = πr²
line: The r slides free, π peels off to divide, a square root wraps A/π, then a circle's radius tracks its growing area.

title: Flipping the thermometer formula
line: F = 9/5 C + 32 rearranges into C, then two thermometers sit side by side and moving one drags the other along.

title: Pizza and soda on $20
line: A grid of (pizza, soda) dots lights up green where 3p + s ≤ 20 and crosses out every combo that costs too much.

title: Filling a theater
line: Adult tickets $8, kids $5, at least $400 but only 60 seats: two shaded regions overlap, and a dragged dot shows which mixes work.

title: A square's area becomes a curve
line: A square grows from side 0 to 5 while its area counts up, each size dropping a point that traces out y = x².

title: Doubling past 1000
line: One dot splits into 2, then 4, then 8, the count climbing until it passes 1000 at step 10, solving 2^n = 1024.

title: The catch-up race
line: Runner A starts 30 m ahead at 3 m/s, B runs 5 m/s, and the gap hits zero at 15 seconds.

title: Halves filling a square
line: 1/2, then 1/4, then 1/8 of a square fill in, and the unfilled corner always measures exactly 1/2^n.

title: Shift and subtract
line: S = 1 + 3 + 9 + 27 + 81 sits above 3S shifted one slot, and subtracting wipes out everything except 243 and 1.

title: Rice on a chessboard
line: Bars double on each square, and the running total always lands one grain short of the next square's pile.

title: Finding the lowest point
line: y = x² - 6x + 11 rewrites as (x - 3)² + 2, and the parabola's bottom lights up at (3, 2) as each part is highlighted.

title: Factor to find the zeros
line: x² - x - 6 splits into (x - 3)(x + 2), and dots drop at x = 3 and x = -2 where each factor hits zero.

title: Yearly growth in monthly steps
line: A bar grows 15% in one jump, then a second bar takes 12 small 1.17% jumps and lands at the same height.

title: A square minus a square
line: A 7×7 square loses a 3×3 corner, and the leftover L is cut and slid into a 10×4 rectangle: 49 - 9 = 40.

title: Spotting the hidden squares
line: In x⁴ - 16, x⁴ glows as (x²)² and 16 as 4², it splits into two factors, then x² - 4 splits again.

title: One chunk as a single block
line: In 3(x + 2)² - 5, the (x + 2) becomes one pulsing block, and the value bottoms out at -5 when the block hits 0.

title: Two ways around a rectangle
line: A rectangle's sides unroll into a line, regrouping as L + W twice, then as two L's plus two W's, same length both ways.

title: What the 3 and 2 mean
line: For a phone plan y = 3 + 2x, dragging the 3 slides the line up and down, dragging the 2 tilts it steeper.

title: Starting amount and halving
line: 100 mg of medicine halves each hour as bars shrink, then changing 100 stretches the curve while changing 0.5 changes how fast it drops.

title: Between two doublings
line: 5·2^t steps through 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, then 100 falls between steps, and a log pins it at t ≈ 4.32 on the curve.

title: Counting zeros with logs
line: 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000 sit evenly spaced on a line, and 3000 slides in at position 3.48, solving 10^t = 3000.

title: The slow starter wins
line: y = 100x zooms ahead while 2^x crawls, then at x = 10 the curve blasts past and the axes keep rescaling to hold it.

title: The table that flips
line: Rows of n, n², and 2^n fill in; they tie at 16 when n = 4, then the 2^n column runs away.

title: Two points, one curve
line: From (1, 6) to (3, 54) is ×9 over two steps, so ×3 each step, and y = 2·3^x snaps through both points.

title: Adding stairs vs multiplying stairs
line: Two staircases climb side by side, one adding 3 per step and one doubling, with each step's height shown as its own bar.

title: A sliding window
line: A window 1 unit wide slides along y = 3·2^x and a line; the line's difference stays fixed, the curve's ratio stays exactly 2.

title: Bounces that lose 20%
line: A ball bounces 100, 80, 64, 51.2 cm high, each bounce dropping by the same percent rather than the same amount.

title: Toothpick triangles
line: Triangles join in a row using 3, 5, 7, 9 toothpicks, with +2 arrows between terms and 2n + 1 for jumping straight ahead.

title: Triangles splitting in three
line: Each triangle splits into 3 smaller ones, counting 1, 3, 9, 27, with the ×3 rule on one side and 3^n on the other.

title: Piggy bank shortcut
line: A piggy bank starts at $10 and gains $5 weekly; arrows hop week by week, then one formula leaps straight to week 20: $110.

title: Order matters for machines
line: 4 goes through ×2 then +3 and becomes 11; swap the machines and the same 4 comes out as 14.

title: Stacking two graphs
line: At each x, a bar from y = 2x stacks on a bar from y = x², and the tops trace y = x² + 2x.

title: Table vs graph showdown
line: A table of rising values turns into dots beside a drawn line, and slope triangles on each show which one climbs faster.

title: Three faces of one parabola
line: y = x² - 2x - 8 cycles through factored and vertex forms, and each form lights up its feature: roots, intercept, vertex at (1, -9).

title: Folding the parabola
line: y = (x - 1)² - 9 folds along x = 1, the two halves land on each other, and the roots -2 and 4 meet.

title: Absolute value as a fold
line: The part of y = x - 2 below the x-axis flips up like a hinge, making a V with its tip at (2, 0).

title: Parking meter staircase
line: A clock runs while the parking fee jumps $3 at each new hour, building a staircase of open and closed dots.

title: Half a sideways parabola
line: y = x² flips across the line y = x, the bottom half fades away, and what's left is y = √x.

title: Racing toward an asymptote
line: A dot slides along y = 1/(x - 2) toward x = 2 and shoots upward as its height reads 10, 100, 1000.

title: Slopes of a ball's flight
line: On h = -5t² + 20t, secant lines over each second show average speeds 15, 5, then -5 m/s as the ball rises and falls.

title: The steady ghost car
line: A car lurches 120 km in 2 hours with stops and bursts, while a ghost car at a steady 60 km/h arrives alongside it.

title: Where the fence graph lives
line: A 20 m fence rectangle widens from 0 to 10 m, collapsing flat at both ends, so its area graph lives only between.

title: You can't buy half a ticket
line: A line for $12 tickets breaks apart into separate dots at 1, 2, 3 tickets, since 2.5 tickets isn't a thing.

title: Ferris wheel height
line: A rider circles a Ferris wheel while their height traces a wave beside it, peaking at the top and bottoming out at boarding.

title: Fibonacci squares spiral
line: Squares of side 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 spiral outward, each side the sum of the last two, while dots mark f(n).

title: Triangular numbers stack up
line: Dots stack into triangles of 1, 3, 6, 10, each new row adding n more dots, so T(n) = T(n - 1) + n.

title: Two inputs, one output
line: 3 drops into f(x) = x² - 1 and 8 comes out, -3 also gives 8, and each output lands as a point on the graph.

title: Arrows from inputs to outputs
line: Arrows link students to birthdays; two students sharing a birthday is fine, but one student with two arrows turns red.

title: Units cancel like fractions
line: 60 miles/hour × 3 hours: the hours on top and bottom strike each other out, leaving 180 miles.

title: Same data, scary axis
line: A rise from 96 to 98 looks flat on a 0 to 100 axis, then the axis restarts at 95 and it looks huge.

title: Rational plus irrational
line: Pretend 1/2 + √2 is a fraction, slide the 1/2 over, and √2 ends up a fraction too, which flashes red: impossible.

title: 8 to the two-thirds
line: 8 splits into three groups as 2·2·2, the cube root keeps one 2, squaring it gives 4, so 8^(2/3) = 4.

title: √50 from squares
line: 50 dots rearrange into two 5×5 squares, so √50 pulls out a 5 and leaves √2 behind.

title: Halfway between 1 and 9
line: Exponents 0, 1, 2 map to 1, 9, 81, and the jump from 1 to 9 splits into two ×3 steps, so 9^(1/2) = 3.

title: Filling gaps on 2^x
line: Dots at 2^0, 2^1, 2^2 sit on a curve, then 2^(1/2) = 1.414 and 2^(1/3) = 1.26 drop in, landing exactly on it.

title: The hidden sun
line: Ice cream sales and sunburns rise together month by month, then a sun slides in with arrows to both: it caused each one.

title: Watching r tighten
line: A cloud of 30 points squeezes onto a line as r climbs from 0.1 to 0.98, then tips downhill and r goes negative.

title: Five points per hour
line: A fit line y = 5x + 60 over study-hours data steps one hour right, a brace shows +5 points, and 60 marks zero hours.

title: Residuals as springs
line: Vertical springs join each point to a line; as the line turns, the springs stretch and squeeze until their total settles at its lowest.

title: The residual smile
line: A line fits curved data, the residuals drop onto their own axis, and they form a U-shape that shows the line was wrong.

title: Dots sort into a table
line: Fifty dots (cats or dogs, grade 9 or 10) fly into four cells, counts tally up, then one row turns into percentages.

title: Pegs build a bell
line: Balls bounce left or right through rows of pegs, piling into bins that form a bell, then the middle 68% shades in.
Shading on a normal curve centered at 70 widens one, two, then three spreads out, the percent counting 68, 95, 99.7.

title: Same center, different spread
line: Two dot plots both average 50, but one bunches up and one spreads out, and their standard deviation bars stretch to match.

title: Fencing the biggest pen
line: A rectangle of 40 m fence slides its width from 1 to 19 while the area counter climbs, peaks at 100, then falls.

title: The cheapest soup can
line: A can holding 500 cm³ morphs from tall and skinny to short and wide as a metal-used graph dips to its lowest point.

title: The lifeguard's fastest path
line: A lifeguard runs on sand then swims; the water entry point slides along the shore until the time readout bottoms out.

title: A page grid from squares
line: A page rectangle keeps snipping off squares, each leftover a smaller copy of the page, while the side ratio settles at 1.618.

title: Same crowd, smaller town
line: 100 dots spread over a 10×10 grid squeeze into a 5×5 corner and the people-per-square counter jumps from 1 to 4.

title: Pepperoni per square inch
line: A 10-inch and a 14-inch pizza each get 20 pepperonis, and the bigger pizza's toppings-per-square-inch readout drops to about half.

title: Measuring a lake with circles
line: A wobbly lake outline gets covered by three circles whose areas add up, then the estimate is compared with a grid-square count.

title: A person made of rectangles
line: A stick-figure outline fills in with a circle head and rectangle torso and limbs, each labeled, while a total area counter adds up.

title: Slicing a cone sideways
line: A knife line tilts through a cone drawn from the side while the slice beside it morphs from circle to ellipse to parabola.

title: Spinning a semicircle into a ball
line: A semicircle flips around its diameter like a spinning coin, squashing and stretching, and its ghost copies pile up into a sphere's outline.

title: A hexagon hiding in a cube
line: A slicing plane tilts through a cube and the cut face changes from triangle to square to a perfect hexagon.

title: A ball in a tin can

line: An angle opens from 0 to 2π, the pie slice fills in, and its area counter tracks ½r²θ the whole way.

line: As angle C opens past 90°, the squares on a and b stop filling c's square, and a 2ab cos C strip appears.

line: A flag shape shows a ghost guess for its reflection across y = x, then actually flips and checks the guess.

line: Each corner of a triangle rides its own circle around a center point, sweeping identical 60° arcs.

line: Segments join each point to its reflection, and the mirror line cuts every one at its midpoint at a right angle.

line: The faces 1 to 6 float into circles for 'even' and 'bigger than 3', and the union, overlap and outside light up in turn.

title: Shuffle the labels
line: Twenty plants get their 'fertilized' labels reshuffled 200 times, the gaps pile into a hill, and the real 3 cm gap sits far out.

title: Bigger polls, tighter guesses
line: Polls of 25, 100 and 400 people from a crowd that's 40% blue pile into histograms that get narrower each time the size quadruples.

title: Coin flips pick the groups
line: Sixteen people, some secretly athletes, are split by hand and every athlete lands in one group, then coin flips split them evenly.

title: Tasting the soup
line: One scoop of 100 dots from a jar of 10,000 guesses 27% red, then the jar is revealed to be 30% red.
